title: C# .NET and Oracle Backend
tagline: Build a small book API, one clear step at a time
description: Start with C#, the language used to write your program. Next, learn how ASP.NET Core answers web requests. Practise saving and reading rows in Oracle Database. Then join these skills to build a Reading List API. You will add, read, change and remove books, check mistakes, and test your work on your own computer.
audience: Beginners who want a clear path from their first C# program to a working book API

stages.title: Write your first C# programs
stages.description: Use names, numbers, choices and lists. Learn to write a method, which is a named set of steps. Practise reading a short C# program before you change it.

stages.title: Answer a web request
stages.description: Use ASP.NET Core to make small API routes. A route is an address your program can answer. Send a request and read the JSON data that comes back.

stages.title: Keep data in Oracle Database
stages.description: Read and write small SQL examples. Learn about tables, rows, keys and transactions. These ideas help your book data stay useful after the API stops.

stages.title: Build the Reading List API
stages.description: Connect a .NET API to Oracle. Add a book, list books, change a book and remove it. Check titles, use SQL parameters, test each reply, and try the sample on your computer.

seo.title: C# .NET and Oracle Backend Learning Path
seo.description: Learn C#, ASP.NET Core and Oracle step by step. Build a Reading List API with clear lessons, SQL parameters, validation and practical checks.
